narrativeReportMd:
# xhtml R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No material local breaking change was found for the `xhtml` primitive datatype in the supplied R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions. The local element model remains the same: root `xhtml`, inherited `xhtml.id`, locally prohibited `xhtml.extension`, and required `xhtml.value` with XHTML representation.

## Scope
The comparison used the local core package StructureDefinitions, package indexes, package metadata, and targeted `Element`/`Extension` excerpts to classify inherited snapshot changes. Per the assignment rule, inherited base-artifact changes are not reported as local `xhtml` findings.

## Main migration themes
R4 `xhtml` instances should continue to validate structurally against the R6 `xhtml` datatype where the same XHTML payload rules are assumed. The notable local R6 addition is metadata on the StructureDefinition, especially the `structuredefinition-type-characteristics` value `has-size`, which can matter to tools that consume datatype metadata but does not change instance shape.

## Highest-impact findings
No local hard instance-breaking, likely breaking, critical/high runtime, or critical/high R6-to-R4 representability findings were identified.

## Findings requiring human review
No structured finding requires human review. The main uncertainty is outside the computable StructureDefinition: narrative XHTML subset rules or official change notes could reveal semantic restrictions not encoded in the local datatype artifact.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The local R6 datatype preserved the R4 identity and content model, which is the backward-compatible outcome for existing instance data. Added metadata was represented as StructureDefinition extensions rather than a change to instance elements.

## Follow-up analysis
Base `Element` and `Extension` reports should own inherited snapshot changes such as XPath metadata removal and extension type-domain changes.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No material local breaking change was found for `xhtml`. The canonical identity and element content model are stable; the only notable local R6 change is non-instance metadata such as `has-size`. Confidence is high for StructureDefinition-level compatibility, with a caveat that external narrative XHTML rules were not diffed.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Existing serializers and validators that treat `xhtml.value` as the XHTML payload should not need a structural migration for this datatype. Tooling that reads R6 StructureDefinition metadata may see additional root metadata and should tolerate the new `structuredefinition-type-characteristics` extension. Inherited base-artifact differences should be handled in the `Element` and `Extension` migrations, not as local `xhtml` changes.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for computable StructureDefinition changes because the R4 and R6 artifacts were both present, shared the same identity, and their local differential elements were unchanged. Confidence is lower for any semantic changes documented only in narrative XHTML pages or official change notes, which were not available as primary local inputs.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Both versions use id/name/type `xhtml`, canonical URL `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/xhtml`, `kind` `primitive-type`, base `Element`, derivation `specialization`, status `active`, and `abstract: false`.

Both snapshots contain the same local/inherited element paths: `xhtml`, `xhtml.id`, `xhtml.extension`, and `xhtml.value`. The local differentials contain the same three entries: root `xhtml`, `xhtml.extension`, and `xhtml.value`.

`xhtml.value` remains `http://hl7.org/fhirpath/System.String` with FHIR type metadata `string`. The R6 snapshot also shows inherited FHIR type metadata on `xhtml.id`; because `xhtml.id` is inherited from `Element.id` and absent from the local `xhtml` differential, this is not a local type-domain change.
`xhtml` has no `Reference`-typed element, so no reference target changes apply.
No terminology binding appears on the local `xhtml` elements, so no value set, binding strength, or terminology expansion comparison is applicable.

The local validation shape is unchanged. Snapshot constraint expressions such as `ele-1` are inherited from `Element`, and the observed R4-to-R6 removal of XPath metadata is classified as a base-artifact concern rather than a local `xhtml` finding.
No fixed value, pattern, or default value constraint was found on local `xhtml` elements in either version.
No `minValue`, `maxValue`, `maxLength`, or regex-style value limit changed in the local `xhtml` StructureDefinition content.
All `xhtml` elements with explicit modifier flags remain `isModifier: false`; no modifier reason or modifier semantics were introduced locally.
`xhtml`, `xhtml.id`, `xhtml.extension`, and `xhtml.value` remain non-summary in the compared snapshots.
No slicing is present on the local `xhtml` datatype elements in either version.

The local short/definition text for root `xhtml` and `xhtml.value` remains semantically the same (`XHTML` and `Actual xhtml`). The top-level description changed from `Base StructureDefinition for xhtml Type` to `xhtml Type definition`, which is editorial. Inherited extension wording changed, but that belongs to `Element`/`Extension`; external narrative XHTML subset rules were not diffed.
`xhtml.value` retains `representation: ["xhtml"]`, `min: 1`, `max: "1"`, and string typing. `xhtml.extension` remains prohibited at `0..0`, so no local serialization shape changed.
At the instance level, the R6 datatype has the same required value element and no new local element, type, binding, or cardinality that would prevent representation in R4.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds `structuredefinition-type-characteristics` metadata with value `has-size`
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is metadata on the R6 `StructureDefinition`, not a new element or constraint on `xhtml` instances. It does not make any R4-valid `xhtml` value invalid in R6 and does not add an R6 instance feature that R4 cannot carry.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators and validators that consume R6 datatype metadata should tolerate and, if useful, interpret the `has-size` type characteristic. R4-oriented tools that ignore unknown StructureDefinition extensions should continue to operate on instance data, but strict metadata diff tooling may need to whitelist this expected R6 addition.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 updates publication metadata while preserving datatype identity
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds or changes metadata such as `experimental: false`, generated narrative text, jurisdiction, contacts, work-group metadata, description text, date, and package version. These fields describe the specification artifact and do not change the canonical URL, datatype name, base definition, derivation, or instance content model.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Metadata comparison tools should expect these publication-field differences between R4 and the R6 ballot package. They should not be treated as instance migration requirements for `xhtml`.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: The `xhtml` snapshot includes inherited `Element` material, including `ele-1`, `Element.id`, and `Element.extension`. Changes such as XPath metadata removal and inherited wording differences should be assessed in the `Element` report.

The inherited `xhtml.extension` snapshot references `Extension` constraints, but `xhtml.extension` remains locally prohibited at `0..0`. Any `Extension` value-domain or constraint changes should be owned by the `Extension` report.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff narrative was consulted. The conclusion is based on direct comparison of the supplied local computable artifacts.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Compare against an official HL7 R4-to-R6 datatype diff or change log for `xhtml`.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The StructureDefinition records `xhtml.value` as an XHTML-represented string, but XHTML subset rules are often specified in narrative pages rather than fully in the datatype StructureDefinition. A narrative rule change could create semantic or validation differences not visible in this report's primary inputs.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Diff the R4 and R6 narrative specification pages governing FHIR XHTML content, allowed elements/attributes, namespaces, and serialization rules.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: `xhtml` has no terminology binding in the compared StructureDefinitions, so terminology expansion comparison was not applicable and would not be expected to change the local conclusion.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: No terminology expansion is needed unless another artifact introduces a profile-specific binding on an `xhtml`-typed element.
